options: GiftCard is a copy of Product's file
GiftCard is a kind of Product: it inherits all of Product's methods and can change some
GiftCard can only be made after Product is deleted
questions.explain: Product is the parent, GiftCard the child. The child only writes what's different.

questions.q: GiftCard defines needs_delivery(), and so does Product. card.needs_delivery() runs which one?
options: GiftCard's: Python looks in the object's own class first, so the child's version overrides the parent's
questions.explain: Lookup goes: the object's class, then its parent. GiftCard's version is found first.

questions.q: GiftCard doesn't define price_text(). What does card.price_text() do?
options: Uses Product's price_text(), inherited from the parent
questions.explain: Not found in GiftCard, so Python goes up to Product and finds it there.

questions.q: GiftCard has its own __init__ that never calls super().__init__(...). What happens when describe() reads self.name?
options: AttributeError: 'GiftCard' object has no attribute 'name', because the parent's setup never ran
questions.explain: A child __init__ replaces the parent's. Call super().__init__(...) to run the parent's setup too.

questions.q: Which special method decides what print(masala) shows to a customer?
questions.explain: __str__ is for people (print, f-strings); __repr__ is for developers (lists, the REPL).

questions.q: Two separate Product objects, both 'Masala Box'. Without __eq__, what does a == b give?
options: False: the default == asks whether it's the very same object
questions.explain: Define __eq__ to say what 'the same product' means for Bazaar (same name and seller).

questions.q: (Going deeper) After defining __eq__ on Product, {masala} raises TypeError: unhashable type. Why?
options: Defining __eq__ removes the default __hash__; define __hash__ too if products must go in sets or be dict keys
questions.explain: Equal objects must have equal hashes, so Python drops the old one. hash((self.name, self.seller)) is a good __hash__.

questions.q: (Going deeper) A cart holds products. Should Cart inherit from Product?
options: No: a cart HAS products (composition), it isn't a product; keep them in an attribute
Yes, so it can use price_text()
questions.explain: Inheritance is for 'is a' (a gift card is a product). For 'has a', store the objects as attributes.
